where: OpenAlex, harvest run 4: the genus queries, the citation step and the Erebidae vision review (48 works listed; titles and abstract starts screened with tools/views/screen_candidates.py)
harvest titles and abstracts; web search result titles
the harvest found no work citing 10.1016/j.asd.2020.101002 that names Orgyia

the 35 distinct works the four genus queries listed are papers on tussock moth ecology and outbreaks (Douglas-fir tussock moth predators, parasitoids and stand damage), human eye injuries from tussock caterpillar hairs, caterpillar defence and colouration, a laser pest-control system, and eye papers on other moths (Lymantria, Acentria, Mythimna, Grapholita); the only eye papers on an Orgyia species are the two on Orgyia antiqua (European Journal of Entomology 2007, a light and electron microscopy study of the compound eye; Micron 2007, eyes after UV-A exposure, no abstract stored), which are structural studies without electroretinogram or flicker work by title and abstract and sit on the wanted list for acuity_cpd

the Erebidae family review lists tiger-moth diversity and light-pollution studies, a fruit-piercing moth olfaction paper, a species description, insect colour-vision and moth opsin reviews, moth fauna surveys, a nocturnal pollination review, caterpillar countershading, a radar monitoring review and a biofluorescence review; none reports flicker or temporal resolution for an Orgyia species

desk-screen web searches on 2026-10-18 for this trait: Orgyia flicker fusion; tussock moth flicker fusion (WebSearch returns titles and links only; the titles of each search were read and none was opened); the same two searches serve corner_hz, which share their words (desk-screen.md step 2). The nine titles of "Orgyia flicker fusion" were human flicker-fusion and cognition papers (a deep-learning flicker model, a flicker test and cognitive performance, a foveated-graphics model, a synaptic-clock model), a flicker-fusion test patent, an NLM thesaurus profile page, an electrical study of the compound eye of the isopod Ligia, a Newcastle University repository record and one Springer article (10.1007/BF02160841) that came back without a readable title among the generic flicker results. The nine titles of "tussock moth flicker fusion" were the systematic review of critical fusion frequencies (logged on main from oa-3), the Lepidoptera study "Evolutionary constraints on flicker fusion frequency" (10.1007/s00359-020-01429-3; main logs five butterfly species from it, none an Orgyia) with three press or repository pages about it, an essay on flicker fusion, the Newcastle record again on a second address and a student project on fly flicker fusion. None names an Orgyia species with a measurement, and none was opened.

screened.W2441307743: It is a thesis on how temperature and humidity affect the survival of the eye-spotted bud moth Spilonota ocellana (its "frequency" counts extreme weather events) and holds no flicker-fusion measurement for Orgyia.

note: The common-name step was run as a web search (second query) because the harvest ran no common-name query.
